newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end higher, debt trouble rumours hit.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end higher, debt trouble rumours hit.

text.p: South Korean stocks closed slightly higher on Friday after financial failure rumours offset much of the early gains, brokers said.
They said unfounded rumours that many smaller companies were suffering from heavy debts sparked selling towards the close.
"Financial trouble rumours hit share prices of many small companies although there were no detailed scenarios," said Park Byung-moon, research manager of LG Securities.
The index ended 1.22 points higher at a provisional 652.87.
The release of February current account deficit figures had no major impact.

Chipmakers gained on anticipation that the recovery in interntaional memory chip prices would sustain for the time being. Samsung Electronics was up 400 won to 58,400, LG Semicon 500 won to 27,500 and Hyundai Electronics Industries 1,000 won to 38,800.
Hit by the financial trouble rumours, Jinro fell 900 won to end at its daily limit of 10,800 and Shinho Paper lost 30 won to 3,100. But officials of the two companies denied the market speculation.
